title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to have her urologist appointment transcribed by an AI scribe, but the tool falsely recorded that she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms. She found the error in a post-operative letter after kidney stone surgery in March and worried it could affect her workers’ compensation case. After she complained, the urologist apologized, corrected the medical record, and said she would review how AI is used in her practice.

Privacy advocates say such mistakes are common, including wrong cancer locations and false epilepsy diagnoses. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 percent of GPs regularly use AI scribes, though none are approved by the Therapeutic Goods Administration. The regulator has been reviewing these tools and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted upon. Patient groups want approved lists and stronger consent rules.
